title: Fire & Smoke Vision Prototype
summary: Computer-vision experiments and a monitoring interface for detecting visual signs of fire and smoke.
problem: Camera-based monitoring needs to connect visual detection experiments with a clear interface for status, events and alarms.
approach: Explored OpenCV image-processing methods and TensorFlow/Keras models.
Worked with image annotations and dataset-preparation tooling.
Developed monitoring components for camera status, event handling and alarms.
outcome: A prototype workspace connecting vision experiments, embedded-camera integration and an operator-facing monitoring application.
role: Software development, vision experiments and embedded integration

sections.title: A two-stage vision pipeline
body: C++ and OpenCV identify image regions that may contain fire or smoke. A neural-network stage then examines candidate imagery. The prototype brings these detection stages together with an embedded device and an operator interface.

sections.title: Processing close to the camera
body: A Raspberry Pi provides the processing unit near the camera. The hardware design brings camera input, digital I/O and network communication into a compact assembly intended for installation alongside the monitored scene.

sections.title: From detection to operator awareness
body: Detection events feed several output paths: hardware I/O, SMS/GSM, a local browser view and a Windows application. The desktop interface combines live imagery, network/device status and event records.

sections.title: A browser interface for device settings
body: A local HTTP interface exposes configuration and monitoring without a dedicated desktop installation. Its settings cover device status, emergency outputs and SMS-related functions.

sections.title: Hardware development and testing
body: The project includes an enclosed prototype and a CCTV-style assembly with GSM connectivity. Internal hardware photographs, a schematic, interface screenshots and demonstration recordings show how the vision software and physical device were brought together.

strength: From camera input to a complete alert workflow.
contribution: My work covered software development, computer-vision experiments and embedded integration, including monitoring components for camera status, events and alarms.
result: A prototype workspace connecting vision experiments, embedded-camera integration and an operator-facing monitoring application.
decisionNotes: The prototype separates C++/OpenCV candidate-region processing from a neural-network stage, then connects device events to hardware outputs, GSM/SMS and local-network monitoring. A Windows/PyQt application and an HTTP panel expose imagery, status and settings.
validationNotes: The archive contains physical OpenCV fire-test recordings, an indoor detection test, a simulated detection workflow, a schematic, prototype photographs and monitoring-interface views. These document prototype behaviour and integration; no detection-accuracy study, false-alarm measurement or safety certification is supplied.
